question.question:
D1 — Use the job library's retry hooks, or build a custom inline scheduler?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-jikZRT on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: The plan writes its own retry timer inside each of 5 workers even though the job library already ships retry hooks that do the same job. The only stated reason is control over the delay curve, and retry hooks normally let you plug in your own delay function. Writing your own scheduler means you also own attempt counting, persistence of retry state across restarts, and every bug in those.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a hand-rolled scheduler that loses retry state on a worker restart drops or double-runs jobs silently, and you maintain five copies of it.
Recommendation: A because the library hook almost certainly accepts a custom delay function, which gives the curve control the plan wants with none of the scheduling code [Layer 1: proven built-in over reinvention].
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=n/a (investigation only)
Pros / cons:
A) Library retry hooks + custom backoff function (recommended)
  ✅ The library already persists attempt counts and schedules the next run, so restarts do not lose retry state
  ✅ The curve lives in one small pure function that is trivial to unit test and reuse across all 5 workers
  ❌ If the hook does not expose a per-job delay function, you need a shim or a library upgrade before this works
B) Custom inline scheduler in each worker (as planned)
  ✅ Complete control over timing with no dependency on the library's hook semantics
  ✅ No need to learn or verify the library's retry API before starting
  ❌ You own attempt counting, persistence across restarts and the dispatch loop, in five places (human: ~3 days / CC: ~40 min, plus ongoing maintenance)

  ✅ Settles the one open fact (does the hook take a delay function) before committing to either design
  ✅ Cheap: read one library signature and one existing hook usage (human: ~1h / CC: ~5 min)

question.question:
D2 — What delivery guarantee does processWebhookJob keep once it can retry?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-jikZRT on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: Today a webhook is sent at most once: if the send fails, it is dropped, never duplicated. Adding retries flips that. If the request reaches the receiver but the response times out, the retry sends the same webhook again, and the receiver sees two. Receivers that charge a card or create a record on each webhook will do it twice.
Stakes if we pick wrong: duplicate side effects at every customer receiving your webhooks, with no way for them to tell a retry from a new event.
Recommendation: A because an idempotency key plus a persisted delivery record keeps retries safe for receivers and costs one small table or column and one header.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10
Pros / cons:
A) Idempotent delivery with per-job delivery record (recommended)
  ✅ Retries recover from transient receiver outages without ever recording two successful deliveries for one job
  ✅ The `Idempotency-Key` header is the standard way webhook receivers dedupe, so well-built receivers drop the duplicate automatically
  ❌ Needs a persisted delivery-state record (pending / delivered / ambiguous) written before each send, plus a migration (human: ~1 day / CC: ~15 min)
B) Exclude processWebhookJob from the retry framework
  ✅ Preserves today's at-most-once behavior exactly, so the existing contract and its regression test stay simple
  ✅ Smallest change: this worker just does not wire the retry hook
  ❌ Webhooks still vanish on any transient failure, which is the pain this plan exists to fix
C) At-least-once with no dedup
  ✅ Simplest retry wiring; no delivery table and no header
  ✅ Every job eventually delivers or dead-letters
  ❌ Every ambiguous send produces a visible duplicate at the receiver and pushes the dedup burden onto every customer
Net: one header and one state record versus either keeping the drops or shipping duplicates to customers.

options.label: Idempotent delivery + retry (recommended)
options.description: Persist a per-job delivery record (pending / delivered / ambiguous) written before each send; send `Idempotency-Key: <job id>` on every attempt; on retry, skip the send if the record is already `delivered`, otherwise resend with the same key so the receiver can dedupe. Completeness 10/10. Human ~1 day / CC ~15 min. Risk: needs a migration; receivers that ignore the header may still see a duplicate after an ambiguous send, which is the documented limit.

options.label: Exclude webhooks from retries
options.description: Keep processWebhookJob on its current at-most-once path and do not wire the retry hook for it. The other 4 workers retry. Completeness 7/10. Human ~0 / CC ~0. Risk: webhook drops on transient failure continue.

options.label: At-least-once, no dedup
options.description: Wire the retry hook for processWebhookJob with no delivery record and no idempotency header; document to receivers that delivery is at-least-once. Completeness 3/10. Human ~1h / CC ~5 min. Risk: duplicate side effects at receivers.

question.question:
D3 — What happens when a job keeps failing: cap attempts and dead-letter it, cap and drop, or retry forever?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-jikZRT on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: Some jobs will never succeed: a receiver that returns 410 Gone, a payload that fails validation. The plan never says when to stop retrying or where the job goes when you do. Retry forever and those poison jobs sit in the queue burning worker time. Drop them and you lose the evidence of what went wrong. Dead-letter them and someone at 3am can see the job, the last error, and replay it.
Stakes if we pick wrong: either an ever-growing queue of jobs that will never complete, or silently lost work with no record.
Recommendation: A because a finite cap plus a dead-letter set is the standard pattern and most job libraries already ship the dead set, so the cost is one setting and one alert.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=2/10
Pros / cons:
A) Finite max attempts + dead-letter set with alert (recommended)
  ✅ Poison jobs leave the live queue after a bounded number of attempts, so healthy jobs are not starved
  ✅ The dead set keeps the job and its last error, so an operator can inspect and replay instead of guessing
  ❌ Needs a dead set (library-provided or one table) and one alert wired to it (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min)
B) Finite max attempts, discard on exhaustion
  ✅ Bounded retries with the least code: one setting and one error log line
  ✅ No dead-letter storage to operate or prune
  ❌ Exhausted jobs are gone; the only trace is a log line, so replay means re-creating the job by hand
C) Unbounded retries (plan as written)
  ✅ No job is ever declared failed, so nothing needs an operator decision
  ✅ Zero additional code beyond the curve
  ❌ A permanently failing job retries forever, and once the delay cap is hit it consumes a worker slot on every cycle
Net: a few lines of configuration and one alert versus either an unbounded poison queue or silently discarded work.

options.label: Max attempts + dead-letter (recommended)
options.description: Finite max attempts (default 5, per-worker override) on the library retry hook. On exhaustion, move the job and its last error to the library's dead set if it has one, otherwise to a dead-letter table; emit one metric and alert on dead-letter growth. Includes tests for the exhaustion path. Completeness 10/10. Human ~half day / CC ~10 min.

options.label: Max attempts, discard
options.description: Finite max attempts (default 5, per-worker override). On exhaustion, log the job id and last error at error level and drop the job. Includes a test for the exhaustion path. Completeness 6/10. Human ~1h / CC ~5 min. Risk: no replay path.

options.label: Unbounded retries
options.description: No attempt limit; the job retries on the curve until it succeeds. Completeness 2/10. Human ~0 / CC ~0. Risk: poison jobs never leave the queue.

## Original plan (unchanged copy)

```markdown
# Plan: Add background job retry framework

## Architecture
We'll roll a custom exponential-backoff scheduler inline in each worker
rather than use the existing job library's built-in retry hooks. Same
shape as the library version, but we want full control over the curve.

The retry envelope (compute delay, log attempt, dispatch) is duplicated

The existing `processWebhookJob()` flow gets rewritten as part of this
change. No regression test for the prior at-most-once delivery guarantee

On every retry we re-fetch the full job payload from the database, then

graph on the first attempt; not planned.
```
